name: Price-Impact Compression (Amihud)
note: Amihud's ILLIQ - the mean of |log return| divided by dollar volume over illiq_win bars, scaled by 1e6 - is price move per dollar traded, i.e. the SLOPE of the demand curve rather than how far price has already gone. It is ranked against its own trailing pct_hist history to give P_I, and ATR(14)/close is ranked the same way to give P_V. The distinctive cell is the DIVERGENCE: P_I >= p_i with P_V <= p_v, high impact while volatility is ordinary, which says the calm is an absence of participants rather than an absence of disagreement. That arms the setup for arm_win bars; the trade itself needs a directional close (close location in the bar range beyond clv or 1-clv) confirmed by volume at vmult times its 20-bar average, because in a thin book a genuinely sized order travels much further than its size warrants. Exit is a 2*ATR trail, a 10-bar time stop, and an unconditional exit when P_I drops under exit_pi - liquidity has come back and the edge is gone whatever the P&L says.
source: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5(1) - the ILLIQ measure, defined as the daily average of |return| divided by dollar volume. Cited from knowledge; the harvesting agent's attempt to fetch a reference page 404'd. The impact-versus-volatility divergence condition and the entry structure are its synthesis.
